problem: The sentence 'its centroid sits inside the web' is wrong. For a thin-walled channel the centroid lies between the web and the flange tips, on the flange side (about 25 mm from the web centreline for the b = 100 mm, h = 200 mm channel). Saying it sits in the web makes the centroid-to-shear-centre distance look like 37.5 mm when it is about 62.5 mm, and it puts the centroid in the wrong place for the whole chapter.
fix: Replace with: 'A channel is the standard example: its centroid lies between the web and the flange tips, on the flange side, while its shear centre lies outside the section, on the other side of the web.'

problem: Repeats the same error: 'The centroid lies inside the web'. A student who memorises this will draw the centroid on the web centreline and measure the load eccentricity from the wrong point.
fix: Replace with: 'The centroid is not the shear centre for a channel. The centroid lies between the web and the flange tips (about 25 mm from the web centreline in the example), while the shear centre lies outside the section on the other side of the web, 37.5 mm from the web centreline. A load through the centroid still twists the channel.'

where: Quiz Q7 (the same wording appears in worked example step 6)
problem: The answer says 'the shear flow ... is proportional to t'. It is not: q = VQ/I has Q proportional to t and I proportional to t, so q itself is independent of t. Only the first moment of area Q and the second moment of area I are proportional to t. As written, a student would learn the wrong reason for t cancelling.
fix: Answer: 'The first moment of area Q used in q = VQ/I and the second moment of area I are both proportional to t. So t cancels in Q/I: the shear flow, the flange force and hence e do not contain t.' In worked example step 6, say 't appears in Q and in I, so it cancels'.
